chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar — all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn Ghalib, from one who narrated it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Righteous deeds and charity both negate poverty, they both increase the lifespan, and they both repel ninety evil types of death.
And in another narration: And they both repel the evil (type of) death from my Shia.

key_terms.الصَّدَقَةُ: Sadaqa — voluntary charity; monetary or material giving for the sake of God, distinct from the obligatory zakat.
key_terms.الْبِرُّ: Birr — comprehensive goodness, encompassing righteousness, piety, kindness, and virtuous conduct. Broader than mere charity.
key_terms.مِيتَةُ السَّوْءِ: Mitat al-su' — evil/bad death; a death that is sudden, painful, or not accompanied by faith and good deeds.

ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of righteous deeds and charity according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) teaches that performing righteous deeds (birr) and giving charity (sadaqa) bring three spiritual and worldly benefits: negating poverty, extending one's lifespan, and warding off ninety types of evil death. A supplementary narration specifies that these acts particularly protect his Shia followers from an evil death. This teaching encourages believers to engage in acts of goodness and generosity as a means of both worldly protection and divine blessing.
